records.literal_gloss: For the director, with stringed instruments, a maskil of David,

en.L: For the director: with stringed instruments. A maskil of David,
en.B: For the music director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David,
en.R: For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments. A song by David to teach and give insight.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : avec instruments à cordes. Un maskil de David,
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Avec instruments à cordes. Un maskil de David,
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. À jouer sur des instruments à cordes. Un chant de David pour enseigner et faire comprendre.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: kwa ala za nyuzi. Maskili ya Daudi,
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Kwa ala za nyuzi. Maskili ya Daudi,
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Ipigwe kwa ala za nyuzi. Wimbo wa Daudi wa kufundisha na kutia ufahamu.

decisions.choice: The title is verses 1-2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts this psalm's long title as two verses, so the verse numbers here are two higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: stringed instruments: to be accompanied on strings
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, the word (neginot) is used for music played on strings; it tells how the psalm was to be performed.

decisions.choice: maskil: probably a skillful or instructive song
decisions.reason: As in 32:1, the word (maskil) comes from a verb meaning to be wise or to give insight. Its exact sense as a kind of song is no longer known.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The title continues into verse 2, which says when the psalm was written, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: a song to teach and give insight
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the term, as in 42:1.

decisions.choice: "kwa ala za nyuzi" (with stringed instruments) for neginot, translated at every level as the English translates it
decisions.reason: "Ala za nyuzi" is the general Swahili term for instruments with strings; "vinanda" can also mean a keyboard organ to many readers.

source.text: בְּב֣וֹא הַ֭זִּיפִים וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְשָׁא֑וּל הֲלֹ֥א דָ֝וִ֗ד מִסְתַּתֵּ֥ר עִמָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: when came the Ziphites and said to Saul, Is not David hiding himself with us?

en.L: when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, "Is not David hiding himself among us?"
en.B: when the people of Ziph came and said to Saul, "David is hiding among us, is he not?"
en.R: It is from the time when the people of Ziph went to Saul and told him, "David is hiding in our land."

fr.L: quand les Ziphiens vinrent dire à Saül : « David ne se cache-t-il pas parmi nous ? »
fr.B: quand les gens de Ziph vinrent dire à Saül : « David se cache chez nous, n’est-ce pas ? »
fr.R: Il date du moment où les gens de Ziph sont allés dire à Saül : « David se cache dans notre région. »

sw.L: Wazifi walipokuja wakamwambia Sauli, "Je, Daudi hajifichi kwetu?"
sw.B: watu wa Zifu walipokuja na kumwambia Sauli, "Daudi anajificha kwetu, sivyo?"
sw.R: Ni kutoka wakati ule watu wa Zifu walipokwenda kwa Sauli na kumwambia, "Daudi anajificha katika nchi yetu."

decisions.choice: The title is verses 1-2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts this psalm's long title as two verses, so the verse numbers here are two higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the Ziphites: 1 Samuel 23 and 26
decisions.reason: While David was hiding from Saul in the wilderness of Ziph, south of Hebron, the people of Ziph went to Saul and offered to hand him over (1 Samuel 23:19-20). They did the same again later (1 Samuel 26:1). Both times Saul set out after David and David escaped.

decisions.choice: Is not David hiding: a question expecting yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of stating the fact: David is hiding among us.

decisions.choice: the people of Ziph
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the town.

decisions.choice: in our land
decisions.reason: Readable says where David was hiding (m1).

records.literal_gloss: God, by your name save me, and by your might vindicate me.

en.L: God, by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name save me, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might vindicate me.
en.B: God, save me by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; \q by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength take up my cause.
en.R: God, save me, and show everyone who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. \q Use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power to prove that I am in the right.

fr.L: Dieu, par {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom sauve-moi, \q et par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} puissance rends-moi justice.
fr.B: Dieu, sauve-moi par {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ; \q par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} force prends ma défense.
fr.R: Dieu, sauve-moi, et montre à tous qui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es. \q Par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} puissance, montre que j’ai raison.

sw.L: Ee Mungu, kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} uniokoe, \q na kwa uweza {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} unitetee.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, uniokoe kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; \q kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} uitetee haki yangu.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, uniokoe, na uwaonyeshe wote {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani. \q Tumia nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kuonyesha kwamba mimi niko sahihi.

decisions.choice: your name: God himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: God's name stands for who he is and for his reputation (52:11). David asks God to act in a way true to his name.

decisions.choice: vindicate: judge in my favor
decisions.reason: The verb (din) means to judge, and in a prayer like this to decide a case in someone's favor (7:9).

decisions.choice: save me, and show everyone who you are
decisions.reason: Readable says what "by your name" means (m1).

decisions.choice: prove that I am in the right
decisions.reason: Readable says what vindicating means (m2).

records.literal_gloss: God, hear my prayer; give ear to [the] sayings of my mouth.

en.L: God, hear my prayer; \q give ear to the sayings of my mouth.
en.B: God, listen to my prayer; \q pay attention to what I am saying.
en.R: God, hear me when I pray. \q Listen to what I am asking.

fr.L: Dieu, écoute ma prière ; \q prête l’oreille aux paroles de ma bouche.
fr.B: Dieu, écoute ma prière ; \q sois attentif à ce que je dis.
fr.R: Dieu, écoute-moi quand je prie. \q Entends ce que je demande.

sw.L: Ee Mungu, sikia sala yangu; \q tega sikio kwa maneno ya kinywa changu.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, sikiliza sala yangu; \q yasikilize maneno ninayoyasema.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, unisikie ninaposali. \q Sikiliza ninachokuomba.

decisions.choice: give ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: As in 5:2.

decisions.choice: what I am saying (B); what I am asking (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable drop "of my mouth", which English does not need.

source.text: כִּ֤י זָרִ֨ים׀קָ֤מוּ עָלַ֗י וְֽ֭עָרִיצִים בִּקְשׁ֣וּ נַפְשִׁ֑י לֹ֤א שָׂ֨מוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְנֶגְדָּ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless [ones] have sought my soul; not they have set God before them. Selah.

en.L: For strangers have risen up against me, \q and ruthless [men] have sought my soul; \q they have not set God before them. Selah
en.B: For outsiders have risen up against me, \q and violent people are hunting for my life; \q they give God no thought. Selah
en.R: Strangers are attacking me. \q Cruel people are trying to kill me. \q They do not care about God at all. Selah

fr.L: Car des étrangers se sont levés contre moi, \q et des [hommes] violents ont cherché mon âme ; \q ils n’ont pas placé Dieu devant eux. Sélah
fr.B: Car des étrangers se sont dressés contre moi, \q et des gens violents en veulent à ma vie ; \q ils ne se soucient pas de Dieu. Sélah
fr.R: Des étrangers m’attaquent. \q Des gens cruels cherchent à me tuer. \q Ils ne s’occupent pas du tout de Dieu. Sélah

sw.L: Kwa maana wageni wameinuka dhidi yangu, \q na watu wakatili wameitafuta nafsi yangu; \q hawakumweka Mungu mbele yao. Sela
sw.B: Kwa maana watu wa nje wameinuka dhidi yangu, \q na watu wenye jeuri wanayawinda maisha yangu; \q hawamjali Mungu hata kidogo. Sela
sw.R: Wageni wananishambulia. \q Watu wakatili wanajaribu kuniua. \q Hawamjali Mungu hata kidogo. Sela

decisions.choice: strangers
decisions.reason: The Ziphites were from David's own tribe, not foreigners; they acted like strangers to him. Psalm 86:14, an almost identical line, has "the proud" (zedim), a word that differs by one similar letter, and some Hebrew manuscripts and the Aramaic translation read that here too. The words here follow the main Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: sought my soul: tried to kill me
decisions.reason: To seek someone's soul (nefesh) is to seek their life (35:4; 40:15).

decisions.choice: not set God before them: give God no thought
decisions.reason: To set the LORD before oneself is to keep him in mind and live by him (16:8). These men do the opposite.

decisions.choice: my life (B); kill me (R)
decisions.reason: Nefesh here is life itself (m2).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים עֹזֵ֣ר לִ֑י אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י בְּֽסֹמְכֵ֥י נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, God [is] a helper to me; [the] Lord [is] among those who sustain my soul.

en.L: Look, God [is] a helper to me; \q the Lord [is] among those who uphold my soul.
en.B: But see, God comes to my aid; \q the Lord is the one who holds my life up.
en.R: But God helps me! \q The Lord keeps me alive.

fr.L: Voici, Dieu [est] un secours pour moi ; \q le Seigneur [est] parmi ceux qui soutiennent mon âme.
fr.B: Mais voici que Dieu vient à mon aide ; \q le Seigneur est celui qui soutient ma vie.
fr.R: Mais Dieu m’aide ! \q Le Seigneur me garde en vie.

sw.L: Tazama, Mungu [ni] msaidizi wangu; \q Bwana [yu] miongoni mwa wanaoitegemeza nafsi yangu.
sw.B: Lakini tazama, Mungu ananisaidia; \q Bwana ndiye anayeyashikilia maisha yangu.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu ananisaidia! \q Bwana ananiweka hai.

decisions.choice: among those who uphold: the one who upholds
alternatives: the Lord is with those who uphold me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "among those who uphold". This is a Hebrew way of saying what someone is (118:7): the Lord is the one who upholds, not one helper among many.

decisions.choice: the Lord: 'Adonai
decisions.reason: The title 'Adonai means master; it is not the divine name.

decisions.choice: Look: a turn to confidence
decisions.reason: The word (hinneh) points to something new: after the Selah, the prayer turns from danger to trust.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the turn from the enemies of verse 5 to God (m3).

decisions.choice: my life (B); keeps me alive (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.literal_gloss: He will return the evil to my enemies; in your faithfulness destroy them.

en.L: He will bring back the evil on my enemies; \q in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness destroy them.
en.B: He will turn back the harm on my enemies; \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful, wipe them out.
en.R: God will pay back my enemies for the evil they plan. \q You are faithful, so destroy them.

fr.L: Il fera retomber le mal sur mes ennemis ; \q dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fidélité détruis-les.
fr.B: Il fera retomber le mal sur mes ennemis ; \q parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es fidèle, anéantis-les.
fr.R: Dieu fera payer à mes ennemis le mal qu’ils préparent. \q Tu es fidèle, alors détruis-les.

sw.L: Atawarudishia adui zangu ule ubaya; \q kwa uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uwaangamize.
sw.B: Atauelekeza ubaya kwa adui zangu wenyewe; \q kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwaminifu, uwafutilie mbali.
sw.R: Mungu atawalipa adui zangu kwa ubaya wanaoupanga. \q Wewe ni mwaminifu, kwa hiyo uwaangamize.

decisions.choice: He will return: the form to be read
decisions.reason: The written text has "the evil will return to my enemies"; the form to be read has "he will return the evil". The words here follow the form to be read; either way the harm they meant for David falls back on them (7:16-17).

decisions.choice: my enemies: those who watch for my fall
decisions.reason: The word (shorer) is used of enemies who lie in wait (5:9).

decisions.choice: destroy them: a plea for justice left with God
decisions.reason: David does not take revenge; he asks God, who is faithful, to deal with those who hunt for his life (54:5). He had spared Saul himself (1 Samuel 26:9-11).

decisions.choice: your: the prayer speaks to God again
decisions.reason: The verse turns from speaking about God ("he") to speaking to him ("your").

decisions.choice: God ... the evil they plan
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts and whose evil it is (m1).

source.text: בִּנְדָבָ֥ה אֶזְבְּחָה־לָּ֑ךְ א֤וֹדֶה שִּׁמְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to you; I will give thanks to your name, YHWH, for [it is] good.

en.L: Freely I will sacrifice to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q I will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for [it is] good.
en.B: I will offer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a sacrifice of my own free will; \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, for it is good.
en.R: I will gladly give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} an offering. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are good.

fr.L: De bon gré je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sacrifierai ; \q je rendrai grâce à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car [il est] bon.
fr.B: Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}offrirai un sacrifice de mon plein gré ; \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rendrai grâce et j’honorerai {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, car il est bon.
fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donnerai une offrande de tout cœur. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remercierai, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es bon.

sw.L: Kwa hiari nitakutolea {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} dhabihu; \q nitalishukuru jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana [ni] jema.
sw.B: Nitakutolea {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} dhabihu kwa hiari yangu mwenyewe; \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakushukuru na kuliheshimu jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, kwa maana ni jema.
sw.R: Nitakuletea {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} sadaka kwa furaha. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakushukuru, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwema.

decisions.choice: freewill offering: a gift not owed
decisions.reason: A freewill offering (nedavah) was a sacrifice given out of gratitude, not to meet a vow or a duty (Leviticus 7:16).

decisions.choice: for it is good: God's name is good
decisions.reason: As in 52:11, "good" describes God's name, that is, God himself.

decisions.choice: the LORD: the divine name in this psalm
decisions.reason: This is the one place where the psalm uses the divine name; elsewhere it says "God", as the psalms of this part of the book often do.

decisions.choice: Freely (L); of my own free will (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced give the sense of the word for the offering (m1).

decisions.choice: because you are good
alternatives: your name ... for it is good
decisions.reason: Readable says "you" for God's name (m2).

decisions.choice: "SEIGNEUR" without the article when the LORD is addressed, with "Yahvé" as the alternative
decisions.reason: In address French drops the article, as it does with "Seigneur"; the capitals still mark the divine name.

source.text: כִּ֣י מִכָּל־צָ֭רָה הִצִּילָ֑נִי וּ֝בְאֹיְבַ֗י רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For from every trouble he has delivered me, and on my enemies has looked my eye.

en.L: For from every trouble {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has rescued me, \q and my eye has looked on my enemies.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has pulled me out of every trouble, \q and my eyes have seen my enemies defeated.
en.R: He has rescued me from every kind of trouble. \q I have seen my enemies beaten.

fr.L: Car de toute détresse {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a délivré, \q et mon œil a regardé mes ennemis.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a tiré de toute détresse, \q et mes yeux ont vu mes ennemis vaincus.
fr.R: Il m’a sauvé de toutes sortes de malheurs. \q J’ai vu mes ennemis battus.

sw.L: Kwa maana kutoka kila taabu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ameniokoa, \q na jicho langu limewatazama adui zangu.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} amenitoa katika kila taabu, \q na macho yangu yamewaona adui zangu wakishindwa.
sw.R: Ameniokoa kutoka kila aina ya taabu. \q Nimewaona adui zangu wakishindwa.

decisions.choice: he has delivered me: God, or God's name
decisions.reason: The verb may have God as its subject, or the name praised in verse 8. Either way God is the rescuer. The past form speaks of the rescue as done.

decisions.choice: my eye has looked on my enemies: I have seen their defeat
decisions.reason: To look on one's enemies is to see them beaten (59:11; 92:12; 118:7).

decisions.choice: defeated (B); beaten (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the eye saw (m2).
